question.worked_solution:
We have $\frac{1}{8}$ on the left and $\frac{3}{8}$ on the right.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14129500/assets/abab6ca3b021dd1a8d38ea55008707c374f03e52b930fa3fa6dd187fe7945047.png)

The shape on the left has $1$ shaded piece, and the shape on the right has $3$ shaded pieces. So, the number of shaded pieces has increased by a factor of $3.$

Therefore, we have

$$
\frac{1}{8}\times 3=\frac{3}{8}.
$$

So, the missing number is $3.$
